name: Fine Print Decoder
why_it_works: Jargon makes people feel shut out, and a little embarrassed to ask. Translating the scary words on a document they already hold gives instant relief, and people save a decoder to use later, which keeps the brand in their camera roll right when the document shows up.

hook.pattern: Name a document people get but never understand, and promise to translate the words that matter.
examples: Signing your {{document_name}}? Read these 4 words first.

variables.name: meaning_1
variables.description: Plain-language meaning of term 1, one or two sentences
variables.example: The yearly cost of the loan including fees, not just the interest rate. Compare this number between lenders.

variables.name: meaning_2
variables.example: An account that holds money for your property taxes and insurance, paid with your monthly payment.

variables.name: meaning_3
variables.example: Fees you can pay upfront to lower your rate. Worth it only if you keep the loan long enough.

variables.name: term_4
variables.description: Fourth jargon term, ideally the one that surprises people

variables.name: meaning_4
variables.example: A charge for paying the loan off early. Ask if your loan has one before you sign.

variables.name: offer
variables.example: Send us your Loan Estimate and we'll review it free

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, from the matching pack in compliance/packs.json
variables.example: Not financial advice. Terms apply. NMLS # shown.

cta: Save this for when your {{document_name}} arrives. {{offer}}.

slides.headline: Your {{document_name}}, decoded
slides.body: 4 words that matter. Save this before you sign.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 overhead photo of a printed {{document_name}} on a wooden desk with a pen and reading glasses, soft window light, a magnifying glass over one line

slides.headline: {{term_1}}
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 dictionary-style card in {{brand}} colors with the word '{{term_1}}' large and a highlighted line on a blurred document behind

slides.headline: {{term_2}}
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 dictionary-style card in {{brand}} colors with the word '{{term_2}}' large and a highlighted line on a blurred document behind

slides.headline: {{term_3}}
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 dictionary-style card in {{brand}} colors with the word '{{term_3}}' large and a highlighted line on a blurred document behind

slides.headline: {{term_4}}: the one people miss
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 dictionary-style card with the word '{{term_4}}' large and a red underline, a warning-yellow highlight on a blurred document behind

slides.headline: Still confused? That's normal.
slides.body: Most fine print is written for whoever drafted it, not for you.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 candid photo of a person at a kitchen table reading the {{document_name}} with a relieved expression, warm lamp light

slides.headline: Get a second set of eyes
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 clean {{brand}} logo card with the offer in large type and a save bookmark icon

craft.notes: Every term slide uses the identical layout so the swipe rhythm feels like flipping flashcards. Order terms from familiar to surprising, and put the one that costs people money last so the swipe has a payoff. Each meaning ends with a 'what to do' clause, not just a definition.

do_not: Give a definition so lawyerly it needs its own decoder
Choose terms nobody actually sees on the real document
Turn the last slide into a hard sell; the help offer should feel like a favor
compliance: Law firm: 'General information, not legal advice'; label attorney advertising where required; no promises about outcomes of any contract dispute
Mortgage: show the NMLS number and lender disclosures; do not quote specific rates or savings in definitions
Insurance: 'Coverage varies by policy; read your policy documents'; show agent license where required
